title: Relative dimension at a point of the target equals the fibre dimension for maps of spaces
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S and a point y of |Y|, the lemma identifies two numbers: the minimal d such that f has relative dimension <= d at every point over y (with d = -infinity off the image), and the dimension of the fibre X_k for any field-valued point in the class y. The retained proof is a fully written chart descent: choose an affine etale V -> Y with v over y, extract from the surjective etale map V x_Y Spec(k) -> Spec(k) a finite separable extension k'/k and the cartesian diagram of spectra (cited Properties of Spaces lemma points-cartesian and Morphisms lemma etale-over-field), replace X -> Y by the V-base change and X_k by X_{k'} justifying invariance of both numbers through the two cited dimension lemmas (dimension-decent-invariant-under-etale, dimension-fibre-after-base-change), reduce to k = kappa(y), then take a surjective etale affine scheme U -> X and conclude dim(X_k) = dim(U_k) = max dim_u(U_k) equals the relative-dimension bound by definition. Retained author proof at lines 7137-7180.
